title: Dyslipidaemia: risk categories, LDL-C goals and lipid-lowering therapy
subject: cardiology
setting: Outpatient clinic, primary care, post-ACS discharge
summary: Classify cardiovascular risk, set a risk-based LDL-C goal (below 55 mg/dL (1.4 mmol/L) with at least 50% reduction for very high risk), start a statin at the right intensity, then add ezetimibe and a PCSK9 inhibitor or inclisiran if not at goal; measure Lp(a) once and check lipids 4 to 12 weeks after each change.

sections.title: Assess cardiovascular risk (ESC/EAS)
items: Very high risk: documented ASCVD (clinical or unequivocal on imaging); diabetes with target organ damage, 3 or more major risk factors or type 1 diabetes for over 20 years; eGFR below 30; familial hypercholesterolaemia with ASCVD or another major risk factor; very high SCORE2 or SCORE2-OP estimate.

High risk: a single markedly raised risk factor (total cholesterol above 310 mg/dL (8 mmol/L), LDL-C above 190 mg/dL (4.9 mmol/L) or BP 180/110 mmHg or more); FH without other risk factors; diabetes for 10 years or more without organ damage; eGFR 30 to 59; high SCORE2 estimate.

Otherwise estimate 10-year risk with SCORE2 (age 40 to 69) or SCORE2-OP (70 or older) using age-specific thresholds; ACC/AHA 2026 uses the PREVENT calculator (borderline 3 to under 5%, intermediate 5 to under 10%, high 10% or more).

Risk enhancers: South Asian ancestry, Lp(a) above 50 mg/dL (about 105 nmol/L), family history of premature ASCVD, CKD, chronic inflammatory disease, HIV, premature menopause or pre-eclampsia history, coronary artery calcium.

sections.title: Investigations
items: Lipid profile (non-fasting is acceptable): total cholesterol, LDL-C, HDL-C, triglycerides, non-HDL-C. If triglycerides are above 400 mg/dL (4.5 mmol/L), use direct LDL-C or apoB rather than the Friedewald formula.
Measure Lp(a) at least once in every adult. ApoB is useful with high triglycerides, diabetes, obesity or very low LDL-C.
Exclude secondary causes: TSH, HbA1c or fasting glucose, creatinine and eGFR, urine protein, liver function, alcohol and drugs (steroids, antiretrovirals, isotretinoin).
Baseline ALT; CK only if muscle symptoms or high risk of myopathy.

Suspect familial hypercholesterolaemia if LDL-C is 190 mg/dL (4.9 mmol/L) or more in adults, tendon xanthomas or premature ASCVD; score with the Dutch Lipid Clinic Network criteria and offer cascade testing of relatives.

sections.title: LDL-C goals
items: ESC/EAS very high risk: LDL-C below 55 mg/dL (1.4 mmol/L) and at least 50% reduction from baseline. Recurrent vascular event within 2 years on maximal statin: below 40 mg/dL (1.0 mmol/L) may be considered.
High risk: below 70 mg/dL (1.8 mmol/L) and at least 50% reduction. Moderate risk: below 100 mg/dL (2.6 mmol/L). Low risk: below 116 mg/dL (3.0 mmol/L).

ACC/AHA 2026 restored goals: below 55 mg/dL for secondary prevention, below 70 mg/dL (non-HDL-C below 100) for high-risk primary prevention, below 100 mg/dL (non-HDL-C below 130) for borderline or intermediate risk.
Secondary goal: non-HDL-C 30 mg/dL (0.8 mmol/L) above the LDL-C goal.

sections.title: Drug therapy
items: Lifestyle for all: stop tobacco, diet low in saturated and trans fat (limit ghee, vanaspati, fried foods), more fibre, regular exercise, weight loss, limit alcohol.

Statin first line. High intensity (about 50% LDL-C lowering): atorvastatin 40 to 80 mg or rosuvastatin 20 to 40 mg. Moderate intensity (30 to 49%): atorvastatin 10 to 20 mg, rosuvastatin 5 to 10 mg, simvastatin 20 to 40 mg.
Not at goal on the maximally tolerated statin: add ezetimibe 10 mg. Still not at goal (very high or high risk): add a PCSK9 monoclonal antibody or inclisiran.
Start statin plus ezetimibe together when the baseline LDL-C is too high for a statin alone to reach the goal, including during an ACS admission.

Statin intolerance: most muscle symptoms are not caused by the statin; rechallenge with a lower dose, a different statin or alternate-day dosing. Use ezetimibe, bempedoic acid or PCSK9-targeted therapy if a statin is truly not tolerated.

Triglycerides 500 mg/dL (5.6 mmol/L) or more: treat secondary causes, restrict alcohol and fat, and add fenofibrate to reduce pancreatitis risk. High-risk patients on a statin with triglycerides 135 to 499 mg/dL (1.5 to 5.6 mmol/L): icosapent ethyl where available.

sections.title: Monitoring
items: Lipid profile 4 to 12 weeks after starting or changing therapy, then every 6 to 12 months once at goal.
ALT once 8 to 12 weeks after starting or increasing a statin; routine repeats are not needed. Persistent ALT above 3 times the upper limit: reduce or stop and investigate.
CK only if muscle symptoms: above 4 times the upper limit with symptoms, stop the statin; above 10 times, stop and check renal function for rhabdomyolysis.
Check adherence before escalating therapy.

sections.title: Special groups
items: ACS: high-intensity statin in hospital whatever the baseline LDL-C; recheck at 4 to 6 weeks and intensify.
CKD not on dialysis: statin or statin plus ezetimibe; do not start statins in patients already on dialysis without ASCVD. Rosuvastatin in CrCl below 30 mL/min: start 5 mg, maximum 10 mg.
Pregnancy and breastfeeding: stop statins when planning pregnancy; bile acid sequestrants if treatment is essential.
Asian patients have higher rosuvastatin exposure (the EU label contraindicates 40 mg); atorvastatin 40 to 80 mg or rosuvastatin 20 mg are common high-intensity choices.
Older adults: continue statins in secondary prevention; in primary prevention over 70 to 75 years, individualise by risk, frailty and life expectancy.

sections.title: Pitfalls
items: Treating to the laboratory reference range instead of a risk-based goal.
Using a low-intensity statin after MI or not intensifying when the goal is missed.
Combining a statin with gemfibrozil (myopathy); use fenofibrate if a fibrate is needed.
Statin interactions: clarithromycin, azole antifungals, ciclosporin, some antiretrovirals; limit simvastatin dose with amlodipine, diltiazem, verapamil or amiodarone.

drugs.name: Atorvastatin
drugs.dose: 10 to 80 mg orally once daily; high intensity 40 to 80 mg

drugs.name: Rosuvastatin
drugs.dose: 5 to 40 mg orally once daily; high intensity 20 to 40 mg
drugs.notes: CrCl below 30 mL/min: start 5 mg, maximum 10 mg. Higher exposure in Asian patients.

drugs.name: Ezetimibe
drugs.notes: About 20 to 25% additional LDL-C lowering. Fixed-dose combinations with statins are available.

drugs.name: Evolocumab
drugs.dose: 140 mg SC every 2 weeks or 420 mg SC once monthly
drugs.notes: Very high or high risk not at goal on statin plus ezetimibe, or FH.

drugs.name: Alirocumab
drugs.dose: 75 or 150 mg SC every 2 weeks, or 300 mg SC every 4 weeks

drugs.name: Inclisiran
drugs.dose: 284 mg SC at 0 and 3 months, then every 6 months

drugs.name: Bempedoic acid
drugs.dose: 180 mg orally once daily (alone or with ezetimibe 10 mg)
drugs.notes: Statin intolerance. Raises uric acid; gout risk.

drugs.name: Fenofibrate
drugs.dose: 145 to 160 mg orally once daily (dose depends on formulation)
drugs.notes: Triglycerides 500 mg/dL (5.6 mmol/L) or more. Reduce dose in CKD; avoid in severe renal impairment.

drugs.name: Icosapent ethyl
drugs.dose: 2 g orally twice daily with food
drugs.notes: High-risk patients on a statin with triglycerides 135 to 499 mg/dL. AF and bleeding risk slightly increased.
